A colossal dark asteroid carved open into stepped terraces, floodlight towers blazing across the scarred rock face, ore conveyors and gantries bolted into the stone, dust hanging in the harsh beams.
A grimy refinery platform clamped to a slowly spinning rock, its tangle of pipework, smelters and fuel tanks glowing orange, battered ore-haulers docked at scaffolded berths.
The hollowed-out interior of a mined asteroid, a cathedral-sized cavern of bare rock laced with catwalks, cabling and machinery, floodlights throwing long shadows across the dusty void.
A rotary drill-rig the size of a building biting a deep shaft into black rock, its derrick crusted with mineral deposits, exhaust venting in dirty clouds under work-lamps yellowed by years of grime.

A strip-mined asteroid reduced to a flat scarred plain, a squat processing plant bolted dead-centre, conveyor belts running ore to hoppers under banks of stuttering floodlights, the rock face eaten back to raw stone.

A swarm of battered mining drones working a fractured ore face, their cutting lasers scoring bright lines across the dark rock, debris tumbling slowly in the void while a supervisor pod hovers at the edge of the light.

An ore-loading dock bolted to the blunt end of a tumbling rock, dented haulers clamped to corroded berths, loaders shovelling crushed ore into cargo holds under harsh arc-lamps, the dock floor thick with grey dust.

A smelter platform glowing furnace-orange against the black, its crucibles pouring molten metal into molds, the whole structure blackened and heat-warped, pipes weeping steam, workers in scarred suits moving through the amber glare.

A quarry pit gouged deep into a rocky planetoid, terraced walls blasted and scraped raw, yellow excavator-rigs working the lowest level under floodlights, ore buckets climbing a chain-lift up the scarred face.

A scaffolded mine-head clamped over a vertical shaft, winch-gear grinding as ore cages rise dripping from the dark below, the framework patched with weld-splatter and tie-wire, a single warning lamp blinking red in the dust.

A long ore-conveyor stretching across a fractured asteroid surface, its steel frame bolted into raw rock, belt running heavy with grey rubble, floodlights on steel poles casting hard shadows across the pitted ground.

A pressurised cutting-bay carved into living rock, plasma-cutters mounted on crawler frames slicing into a mineral seam, the walls black with carbon scoring, ventilation ducts rattling overhead in the thick metallic air.

A battered mobile ore-crusher rolling on wide tracks across broken terrain, its jaws grinding rock to gravel, exhaust stack belching dark particulate, floodlights mounted fore and aft punching through the hanging mineral dust.

A deep-bore tunnel bored horizontally into an asteroid's core, track-mounted ore cars rattling out of the darkness loaded with crushed rock, the tunnel walls slick with mineral seepage, bare bulkhead lamps every thirty metres.

A fuel-and-maintenance depot bolted to a flat-faced rock, rows of patched work-pods docked under corrugated awnings, fuel hoses coiled on rusted reels, the whole installation lit by floodlamps on tilting poles, shadows shifting slowly.

A rock-face blasting operation, drill-holes packed and wired across a broad ore seam, safety lights strobing amber as the blast crew retreats, the scarred wall fractured and glittering under the hard work-lamp beams.

A gravity-drum ore-sorter spinning at the heart of a processing platform, vibrating screens and chutes sorting crushed rock by density, the structure shaking constantly, bolts loose and re-tightened so many times the steel is worn bright.

A suspended cat-walk network inside a partially hollowed asteroid, workers in heavy suits moving between drilling rigs on mesh walkways, the cave walls glistening with ore veins, floodlights mounted on the rock itself throwing raw white light.

A tethered rock-anchor station, massive cable-bolt rigs screwing anchor points into the skin of a tumbling asteroid, the rigs scarred and chipped, work-lamps swinging on their mounts as the rock shifts slowly beneath them.

A mag-locked ore-barge filling at a loading chute, its wide cargo deck open to vacuum, automated shovels packing the hold with loose ore, the barge hull dented and patch-welded, dock lights throwing orange pools across the grime.

A surface-crawling mining rig straddling a narrow ore ridge, its cutting drums grinding the rock below its belly, collection hoppers overflowing, the chassis flexing over the fractured terrain under portable floodlights mounted on its superstructure.

A pressurised habitat dome bolted to a working mine-site, its exterior crusted with mineral dust and impact scars, umbilicals running to the shaft-head, floodlights illuminating the worn airlock and the boot-scrape plates outside its door.

A flotilla of ore-processing barges clustered around a fractured asteroid, connected by gangways and cargo lines, each platform running its own crushers and smelters, the whole assembly lit orange and white against the black, trailing steam.

A rock-anchor winch platform dragging a slow-spinning asteroid into alignment, the winch housings groaning, cable thick as a man's torso under tension, work-lamps clamped to the platform rail casting shaking light across the pitted rock surface.

An emergency patch-repair site on a fractured mine-shaft collar, arc-welders burning bright against the dark, scaffolding hastily erected across the cracked superstructure, the ground around the collar scattered with tools and scorched ore debris under glaring portable floods.
